newsitem.title: RUSSIA: UES, Gazprom, Surgut lead calm Russia shares.
newsitem.headline: UES, Gazprom, Surgut lead calm Russia shares.

text.p: Top Russian shares edged down on Friday after rising on early demand, especially for utility UES, gas monopoly Gazprom, and oil group Surgutneftegaz, dealer said.
At 1100 GMT the 23-share Russian Trading System index was 336.56 after opening at 337.45 and closing on Thursday at 337.38.
Surgutneftegaz preferred at 1200 GMT was $0.580 after an early high of $0.599 and $0.579 at Thursday's close. Surgutneftegaz ordinaries were $0.813 after $0.830 from $0.800.
Some traders said Gazprom would rise further after chairman Rem Vyakhirev's said on Thursday that foreign investors were allowed to buy its domestic shares.
Gazprom was $0.635 was above its earlier $0.610 and $0.627 close on Thursday.
"Vyakhirev's statement encouraged investors; they think the plan looks like a real one," said Valeri Levit of Rinaco-Plus.
But many dealers said they were sceptical about the remarks.

Gazprom late on Thursday reiterated that the company would continue to draw a strict distinction between its domestic shares for local investors and shares available for non-residents in the form of American Depositary Shares (ADSs).

Gazprom said non-residents could buy and trade the domestic shares through local companies, and even make a profit from them, but they could not take the shares abroad, and Gazprom said it would act against any attempt to undermine the ADSs, which trade at a large premium to domestic shares.
Dealers said President Boris Yeltsin's radio comments on Friday that he doubted the 1997 budget could be fulfilled pushed some prices down.
"It is negative news," Levit said. "It is unlikely to support demand."
